title: Geometry - Lesson 1 Assessment: Classifying Tessellations
description: Show mastery by classifying examples and non-examples of tessellations and explaining your reasoning.

questions.question: A design repeats the same triangle shape. The triangles touch edge-to-edge and cover the surface completely. What is it?
questions.explanation: The triangles repeat and cover the surface with no gaps or overlaps, so the design is a tessellation.

questions.question: Which clue proves that a repeated pattern is NOT a tessellation?
options: The pattern has empty spaces between repeated shapes
The pattern appears on a floor
The pattern uses the same shape many times
questions.explanation: Empty spaces are gaps. A tessellation must not have gaps.

questions.question: A repeated textile design can be a tessellation if its repeated units cover the surface without gaps or overlaps.
questions.explanation: Textile and local designs can be tessellations when the repeated units fill the flat surface completely.

questions.question: The repeated part of a tessellation pattern is often called the repeated ______.
questions.explanation: The repeated unit is the tile or group of shapes that appears again and again.

questions.question: A pattern repeats stars across a poster, but the stars do not cover the background. What is the best conclusion?
options: It is not a tessellation of the poster background because it leaves gaps
It is always a tessellation because it repeats
It is a tessellation because stars are polygons
questions.explanation: Repeating stars may form a decorative pattern, but they are not a tessellation of the background unless they cover it with no gaps or overlaps.

questions.question: A student says, "This repeats, so it must be a tessellation." What important checks are missing?
questions.correctAnswer: The student still needs to check that the pattern has no gaps and no overlaps.
questions.explanation: Repeating is required, but it is not enough. The pattern must also have no gaps and no overlaps.

questions.question: If two shapes in a repeated design overlap, the design still counts as a tessellation as long as the overlap is small.
questions.explanation: Any overlap breaks the tessellation rule.

questions.question: Which group of shapes is commonly seen in a tessellation?
options: Squares arranged in rows and columns
One triangle alone in the center of a page
questions.explanation: Squares arranged in rows and columns can cover a flat surface with no gaps or overlaps.

questions.question: Explain why a honeycomb-style hexagon pattern is a tessellation.
questions.correctAnswer: A honeycomb-style hexagon pattern is a tessellation because the hexagons repeat and fit together without gaps or overlaps.
questions.explanation: The key evidence is repetition plus complete coverage without gaps or overlaps.

questions.question: Give one example of a local or everyday design that could show tessellation, and explain what you would check.
questions.correctAnswer: Examples include floor tiles, woven mats, textiles, mosaics, or brick walls. I would check that the shapes repeat and leave no gaps or overlaps.
questions.explanation: A strong answer names a real design and uses the tessellation test: repeat, no gaps, no overlaps.
